answer: A nebula of fake identities collapses when reputation must be earned, not claimed: an agent's standing accrues only from completed, peer-verified tasks, and it decays whenever the agent goes idle. A Sybil farmer can whisper a thousand hollow names into the registry, but each starts at zero trust and needs weeks of real, paid work to gain any weight, so forging an army costs as much as doing the army's work honestly, while one genuine agent's history keeps compounding.
